title: otel span-timing test fails under the full suite, passes alone
rawReport:
## Summary
One test in the tea package's OpenTelemetry suite fails when the whole `pnpm test` run executes, but passes when its file runs by itself. It reproduces on a clean main, so it is not caused by any open PR.

## What I was doing
Driving lane #356 (PR https://github.com/kamp-us/demlik/pull/365). The builder ran the repo-root gates `pnpm typecheck && pnpm typecheck:test && pnpm lint && pnpm test` in its worktree.

## What I observed
`packages/tea/src/otel/otel.test.ts` › "times each span by the transitions that opened and closed it" fails when the full suite runs. The builder reproduced the same failure on a clean checkout of `origin/main` at a5dc8c2. Running that file alone passes. This was reported by the builder shell and not re-run by the operator.

## Why it matters
If CI runs into the same thing, unrelated PRs go red and spend repair rounds on a test they never touched. It could be a timing assertion that is sensitive to load, or state shared between test files.

## Pointers
- packages/tea/src/otel/otel.test.ts
- commit 039b3de (feat(agent): trace an agent run as OpenTelemetry spans (#331))
- PR https://github.com/kamp-us/demlik/pull/365

## Suggested next step (non-binding)
Check whether the span timing assertion depends on wall-clock time or on a global tracer provider that other test files also set.

---

## Summary

`traceAgent` (`packages/tea/src/otel/index.ts`) hands OpenTelemetry the run's clock value `at` as a bare `number` for every `startTime` and `span.end(at)`. `@opentelemetry/sdk-trace` (`Span#_getTime`) reads a numeric time that is `<= performance.now()` as a **performance-relative** timestamp and adds `performance.timeOrigin`; only a number bigger than `performance.now()` is read as epoch ms. So the same `at` means two different instants depending on how long the process has been up.

That is why the test flips. `otel.test.ts`'s `traced()` clock starts at `1_000`. Run alone, the worker reaches the test before `performance.now()` passes 1000 ms, so the root span starts at `[1, 0]`. In the full `pnpm test` run the worker has been busy longer than 1 s, so `1000` is read as "1 s after process start" and the root starts at about `[now, …]`, which fails `expect(root.startTime).toEqual([1, 0])` in "times each span by the transitions that opened and closed it".

Triage note: I reproduced the mechanism directly against the installed `@opentelemetry/sdk-trace-base` 2.11.0. `startSpan("x", { startTime: 1000 })` returned `[1, 0]` at `performance.now()` ≈ 56 ms, and `[1790279771, 847951905]` after a 1.2 s busy-wait. It is not a shared global provider: the test builds its own `BasicTracerProvider` per call and registers nothing globally, and it uses no fake timers. CI's `build` job is green on main because the job is fast enough to stay under the 1 s line. Local builder gates are slower and go red, which is how it hit lane #356.

This is a library bug as well as a flaky test, and it shipped in 0.18.0. Any host whose `clock` returns small values (a logical or test clock, `performance.now()`, a clock offset from process start) gets span times silently rebased onto process start. A `Date.now()` clock hides the bug only because epoch ms is always bigger than `performance.now()`.

Triage note: dedup came back with no match. `report dedup` on "otel span timing flaky test performance.now startTime" surfaced only #335 and #354, which are on other surfaces. Nothing on the board owns `@demlik/tea/otel` timing, so this issue stands alone.

## Scope (v1)

In `packages/tea/src/otel/index.ts`, route every clock value through one conversion to an unambiguous OTel `TimeInput`: an `HrTime` built from the epoch-ms `at` (e.g. `millisToHrTime`-equivalent `[Math.trunc(ms / 1e3), (ms % 1e3) * 1e6]`) or a `Date`. Then no call site can pass a raw `number` to `startTime` or `Span#end`, and OTel never guesses. That covers the `startTime: at` / `startTime: event.at` sites and every `span.end(at)` / `span.end(event.at)` / `brain.end(event.at)`. The mistake-proofing is the single helper: there is exactly one place that turns `at` into OTel time, and it states that `at` is epoch ms.

In `packages/tea/src/otel/otel.test.ts`, make the timing test deterministic whatever the worker's uptime. Start the `traced()` clock at a value that is always below `performance.now()` when the test runs (for example `1`), so the old behaviour always fails and the fixed behaviour always passes. Do not rely on test ordering or on `performance.now()` still being small.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `packages/tea/src/otel/index.ts` passes no bare `number` as a span `startTime` or to `Span#end`; every clock value goes through one helper that converts epoch-ms `at` to an `HrTime` or a `Date`
- [ ] `otel.test.ts` has a test whose run clock starts at a value that is always `<= performance.now()` when it runs (e.g. `1`), and it asserts the root span's `startTime` equals the exact `HrTime` of that epoch-ms value; this test fails against the pre-fix `index.ts`
- [ ] "times each span by the transitions that opened and closed it" still asserts the root starts at the dispatched `at` and every span's end is `>=` its start, and passes whether its file runs alone or under the full `pnpm test`
- [ ] The `traceAgent` doc comment (or the `TraceAgentOptions` / clock docs it points at) says that `at` is read as epoch milliseconds
- [ ] `pnpm typecheck && pnpm typecheck:test && pnpm lint && pnpm test` pass at the repo root

### No-gos

- No retry, `retry:` option, `.skip`, or loosened assertion on the timing test. The fix is the time conversion, not the test's tolerance.
- No change to the `AgentEvent` / `at` shape or the runtime's `clock` contract. The conversion lives in the OTel projection only.
- No global OTel provider or context-manager registration in tests or library code.
- No vitest pool, `isolate`, or `sequence` config changes to hide ordering.
